To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the latent periods of FMDV and ASFV were significantly different for inoculated and contact challenged pigs, (b) ASFV was more transmissible than FMDV, (c) vaccination reduced ASFV transmission by 50-70% but not FMDV transmission, and (d) the infection times of ASFV were longer than those of FMDV.

we have developed a novel method for the inference of epidemiological model parameters from transmission experiments, which accounts for the unobservable infection times and latent and infectious periods, and which can be used for the inference of latent periods, infectious periods, and infectiousness profiles.

(i) we present a Bayesian framework for estimating epidemiological parameters from experimental data that accounts for unobserved processes and (ii) we show that this framework is able to identify the differences between the latent periods and infectious periods of inoculated versus contact-challenged pigs and quantify the effect of vaccination on transmission.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a general methodology to analyse transmission experiments and to provide robust in- ferences about the underlying epidemiological processes.
the development of methods for estimating epidemiological parameters from data collected in transmission experiments and the application of these methods to data from FMDV and ASFV.
the development of a Bayesian framework for inference of epidemiological model parameters from transmission experiments and its application to FMDV and ASFV.

a Bayesian framework is a flexible tool that can be used to fit a range of transmission models to data from transmission experiments, while accounting for the limitations of such data.

the Bayesian approach provides a robust framework for the analysis of experimental transmission data, which allows for more accurate inferences and the identification of important features of the transmission process.
